notes: Some wait classes are not instrumented (mutexes 0 of 246 on, read/write locks 0 of 34 on, shared/exclusive locks 0 of 15 on, priority read/write locks 0 of 2 on, condition waits 0 of 61 on, socket i/o 0 of 7 on), so their waits are not in this report. No mutex or rwlock waits here never means no contention.
1 event(s) were counted but not timed, so they are not ranked: wait/io/socket/sql/client_connection.

Wait time is summed across all threads, background threads included, so it can exceed the wall-clock window. Table I/O includes the file I/O and internal lock waits inside each call, which are counted again under their own events, so the classes are never added up.
InnoDB asynchronous I/O (read-ahead, page cleaner writes) is timed only for submitting the request, so its latency is understated. Bytes are exact (see I/O).
Since server start covers 13 min 38 s of uptime; the longest single wait (max) is since start too, never per window.
